sources.title: Data Processing Addendum — Version 1, August 1, 2026
sources.claimSummary: Schedule 1 describes TLS-protected communications, encryption of network traffic and separation of customer project networks from control-plane networks.
sources.limitation: No explicit mapping to the present upstream connection or explanation of backend ssl=false. This is not HOP_B_PROVEN.

sources.title: Supavisor tenant configuration
sources.claimSummary: Separate controls exist for client SSL enforcement and upstream SSL, certificate verification and CA.
sources.limitation: Open-source fields do not establish current managed tenant values or private-network controls.

sources.title: Supavisor environment variables
sources.claimSummary: Upstream CA and downstream certificate/key paths are separate configuration options.
sources.limitation: No deployment settings or provider secrets obtained.

sources.title: Postgres SSL Enforcement
sources.claimSummary: Incoming Postgres/pooler SSL enforcement is configurable. verify-full verifies CA and hostname; the project CA is available through Dashboard database SSL settings.
sources.limitation: Applies to client policy and CA discovery; does not prove enabled project enforcement or backend-hop settings.

sources.title: SSL enforcement feature
sources.claimSummary: Describes protection for direct and pooler client connections.
sources.limitation: Broad end-to-end wording does not identify the mechanism or explain this backend observation.

sources.title: Supavisor and Connection Terminology Explained
sources.claimSummary: Session mode assigns an underlying database connection exclusively to one client connection.
sources.limitation: Affinity is not upstream encryption, authentication or isolation evidence.

sources.title: Migrate from Postgres to Supabase
sources.claimSummary: Documents session-pooler use for pg_dump/restore and migration work.
sources.limitation: Does not specifically approve this multi-connection exported-snapshot and per-tool proof contract.

sources.title: Connect to your database
sources.claimSummary: Direct is documented for maintenance; session pooling is an IPv4 alternative. Project-specific parameters come from Connect. Direct and pooler usernames differ.
sources.limitation: No actual direct endpoint or network availability for this project can be inferred from templates.

sources.title: Connection pooling and limits
sources.claimSummary: Direct and pooler backend sessions share the database connection budget; services also consume slots.
sources.limitation: Project compute size, configured limits and available maintenance headroom remain unknown.

sources.title: Dedicated IPv4 Address for Ingress
sources.claimSummary: Direct is normally IPv6; an IPv4 add-on is a documented alternative.
sources.limitation: No evidence that this project has the add-on; no purchase/configuration action taken.

sources.title: Self-hosted Docker configuration
sources.limitation: Self-hosted Docker defaults cannot establish hosted project trust.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 snapshot synchronization
sources.claimSummary: Other transactions can import a snapshot while the exporter transaction remains open.
sources.limitation: Requires the relevant database instance and snapshot lifetime; not proof of provider routing or project capacity.

sources.title: Docker host network driver
sources.claimSummary: Linux host-network containers share the host network namespace.
sources.limitation: A bridge network IPv6 flag does not decide the route of this runner host-network container.

classificationRule: EXPLICITLY_APPLICABLE is scoped to the stated claim, not blanket HOP B trust. Only evidence explicitly mapping upstream security could satisfy A3.
reconciliation: Client TLSv1.3 describes runner-to-pooler. Backend pg_stat_ssl=false describes the separate pooler-facing PostgreSQL connection. Both can hold simultaneously. Neither implies encryption/private isolation on the unobserved provider hop.

supportSearch.candidateExplanation: Both hits are our D2 missing-evidence notes, not provider replies.

missingEvidence.exactFactNeeded: Actual managed session-pooler upstream transport, authentication, encryption or alternative protection, private-network boundary and tenant isolation; applicability to this project/service.
missingEvidence.likelyLocation: Attributable support answer or official managed-service architecture statement
missingEvidence.futureProbeNeeded: NO: backend SQL cannot establish hidden provider infrastructure controls.

missingEvidence.exactFactNeeded: Provider explanation of why client TLSv1.3 and backend ssl=false are expected or anomalous for this topology, reconciled with general transit encryption assurances.
missingEvidence.likelyLocation: Same support response referencing the safe historical observations

missingEvidence.exactFactNeeded: Reviewable backup policy binding TLS/identity proof to each psql, pg_dump and pg_dumpall process; accepted proof type and no substitution by a separate handshake.
missingEvidence.whoCanSupply: Project security/operator reviewer, informed by official libpq guarantees

missingEvidence.exactFactNeeded: Sufficient pool/database capacity and timeout policy for one exporter plus one sequential dump connection, including roles dump; snapshot sessions route to the same primary.
missingEvidence.likelyLocation: Project connection settings/metrics export and provider workflow statement
